title: Support crate: Slack-backed ChatBackend bridge
description: Idea from Mark 2026-10-20. Slack has no pluggable transport, so the route is a bridge: a support crate (does I/O) implementing jmap-chat-server ChatBackend on Slack Web API + Events API/Socket Mode, presenting a workspace as a Space. Mapping: workspace->Space, channel->channel Chat, DM/group DM->direct/group Chat, thread->threadRootId, reactions->reactions, basic formatting->rich spans (ccy6). Alternative: two-way relay/puppet bridge (mautrix-slack, matterbridge style). Constraints: bot token sees only joined channels, user OAuth token sees what the user sees; browser session tokens are a ToS grey area, do not use. Rate limits (Slack changelog 2025-05-29): conversations.history/replies dropped to Tier 1 (1 req/min, limit 15) for commercially distributed non-Marketplace apps; internal customer-built apps and Marketplace apps keep Tier 3, so a self-hosted internal app for own workspaces is unaffected. Check docs.slack.dev/apis/web-api/rate-limits before designing history backfill. Workspace admin approval often needed. Huddles, canvases, workflows, Block Kit do not map. Not scheduled; no Rust Bolt SDK, call HTTP APIs directly.
